title: Don't let NTA set paper, scrap General Knowledge, widen access: Expert committee's suggestions for CLAT
description: The Consortium of National Law Universities on Wednesday published the Expert Committee's report on reforming the Common Law Admission Test (CLAT).Although no reforms will apply to CLAT 2027, the report recommends ruling out the National Testing Agency (NTA) as paper-setter, scrapping the exam's General Knowledge section and widening access for candidates who cannot afford coaching.The report was prepared by a five-member Expert Committee that was co-convened by Prof Dev Saif Gangjee of the Univ
